programme.title: Plastic: The Real Sea Monster
programme.desc: Six million metric tons of plastic end up in the world's ocean each year. Unlike other waste, plastic can stay in the water forever without breaking down. How is this deadly killer affecting the world's oceans?

programme.title: Nature's calendar S1 - "January"
programme.desc: For some animals January is a time of lush plenty, for others babies are on their way. From the pine martens that frolic in snowy northern wonderlands to capybara finally released from the Amazon’s dry season to a river swelling with watery life.

programme.title: Nature's calendar S1 - "February"
programme.desc: February is a month of contradictions, where it will be too hot for some and too cold for others. This brings challenges and also unfolding stories – of new life,the fight to protect old ones, battles against the elements and even a little romance.

programme.title: Nature's calendar S1 - "March"

programme.title: Nature's calendar S1 - "April"
programme.desc: For many people April is normally the month of Easter, and similarly in the animal kingdom eggs of all sorts abound. It is a time of new life, a renewal of old ties and, for many creatures, of relief.
